title: Friendship with Jesus (II.8)
hookLine: without a friend you can't live well; let Jesus be your friend
tomorrow: who's still there when the party's over?

lines: A VOICE NOTE FROM FAR AWAY.
THE MASTER IS CALLING FOR YOU.
cards: A voice note from a friend far away. Before the name even loads, the voice is already home: the laugh at the start, the way it says hey. A person can be close to someone they can't see.
The ear knows first. John's Gospel has a moment built on that. A house in Bethany, full of mourners.
A woman sits grieving her brother. Her sister Martha leans close and says quietly that the master is here, and is calling for her. She gets up at once.

teach.b: The Imitation stops right on that moment, in chapter eight of book two. When Jesus is near, it says, all is well and nothing seems hard. When he seems far, everything is hard.
If he speaks just one word, the comfort is great. John calls the woman Mary, Martha's sister; the Imitation, following an older way of reading, calls her Mary Magdalene.
Either way, the point is the rising: one familiar voice, and she's on her feet. Her grief doesn't vanish; she still weeps when she reaches him. But she moves toward the voice.
Then the chapter calls it an art.

teach.h: A GREAT ART: TALKING WITH JESUS.
teach.b: It's a great art, it says, to know how to talk with Jesus, and great wisdom to keep him close. Be humble and peaceable, and he'll be with you; be devout and quiet, and he'll stay.
Then the line at the chapter's heart: without a friend, the book says, you can't live well. It doesn't call loneliness a virtue.

teach.h: WITHOUT A FRIEND YOU CAN'T LIVE WELL.
teach.b: It says if Jesus isn't your friend above all, you'll be very sad and desolate. And its title uses an old word, familiar, in an older sense: close, at home with you, of the household.
Not a distant master you book an appointment with. A friend whose voice you know before the name loads.

how: Many Catholics practice mental prayer, speaking to Christ in their own words as to a friend, and some make a short visit to a church to sit quietly before the tabernacle.

o: Jesus as a close friend you talk with plainly
a well-known friend you've only seen from afar
a formal duty owed to a distant master

s: the Imitation says a holy person can live well without any friend
it says without a friend you can't live well, and asks that Jesus be that friend above all.
John's Gospel calls the woman at Bethany Mary, Martha's sister
the Imitation, following an older reading, calls her Mary Magdalene.
familiar here means someone you've seen around
in the older sense it means close, of the household.

games.q: a friend says prayer feels like leaving a voicemail nobody checks. by chapter eight, what's the Imitation's picture?
o: a familiar friend in the house, kept close by quiet and humility.
a formal appointment you book about once a week.
a test you pass by finding the right words.
games.why: the chapter calls talking with Jesus a great art, and its title calls the friendship familiar: close, at home.

practice: Say a few words out loud, quietly, the way you'd talk to a close friend at the end of a day: one thing that happened, one thing that was hard.
If you pray, say them to Jesus; if you don't, say them to the room and notice how a spoken thought sounds different. Plain words are enough. Then let the quiet answer.

wordCard.voice: Friendship with Jesus. The Imitation's familiar friend: close enough to talk with plainly, and kept near by being humble, peaceable and quiet.

orig.note: Latin, from the title of the Imitation II.8: familiar, close friendship with Jesus.

carryVoice: The line to keep: a familiar friend, close enough that you never have to knock. See you soon.
